projects.title: Big-O Notation Upper Bound Verifier
projects.description: Big-O Notation `O(g(n))` provides a mathematical WORST-CASE UPPER BOUND on algorithm growth. Formal definition: `f(n) is O(g(n))` if there exist positive constants `c` and `n0` such that `0 <= f(n) <= c * g(n)` for all `n >= n0`. Build verifier to find constants `c` and `n0`! In this project, you will build Big-O Upper Bound Verifier in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Big-O Formal Definition, Upper Bound Constants `c` and `n0` & Mathematical Verifications
projects.exampleText: Verify Big-O upper bound for f(n) = 3n^2 + 5n + 10
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Big-O Notation Upper Bound Verifier ---
Verified f(n) = 3n^2 + 5n + 10 <= c * n^2 for c = 4 and n0 = 10 (f(n) is O(n^2)).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Upper Bound Condition**: `f(n) <= c * g(n)` for all `n >= n0`.
2. **Constant Finder**: Find smallest integer constant `c` and threshold `n0`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `big_o_verifier_demo()`: Solves Big-O Notation Upper Bound Verifier.

projects.title: Big-Omega Notation Lower Bound Verifier
projects.description: Big-Omega Notation `Omega(g(n))` provides a mathematical BEST-CASE LOWER BOUND on algorithm growth. Formal definition: `f(n) is Omega(g(n))` if there exist positive constants `c` and `n0` such that `0 <= c * g(n) <= f(n)` for all `n >= n0`. Build verifier for lower bound constants! In this project, you will build Big-Omega Lower Bound Verifier in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Big-Omega Formal Definition, Lower Bound Constants `c` and `n0` & Best-Case Proofs
projects.exampleText: Verify Big-Omega lower bound for f(n) = 2n^2 - 3n
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Big-Omega Notation Lower Bound Verifier ---
Verified f(n) = 2n^2 - 3n >= c * n^2 for c = 1 and n0 = 3 (f(n) is Omega(n^2)).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Lower Bound Condition**: `f(n) >= c * g(n)` for all `n >= n0`.
2. **Lower Bound Constants**: Compute valid constant `c` and threshold `n0`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `big_omega_verifier_demo()`: Solves Big-Omega Notation Lower Bound Verifier.

projects.title: Big-Theta Notation Tight Bound Verifier
projects.description: Big-Theta Notation `Theta(g(n))` provides an TIGHT BOUND (both upper AND lower bound simultaneously!). Formal definition: `f(n) is Theta(g(n))` if `f(n) is O(g(n))` AND `f(n) is Omega(g(n))`: `c1 * g(n) <= f(n) <= c2 * g(n)` for all `n >= n0`. In this project, you will build Big-Theta Tight Bound Verifier in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Big-Theta Tight Bounds, Dual Constants `c1` and `c2` & Exact Asymptotic Sandwiching
projects.exampleText: Verify Big-Theta tight bound for f(n) = 5n^2 + 2n
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Big-Theta Notation Tight Bound Verifier ---
Verified c1 * n^2 <= 5n^2 + 2n <= c2 * n^2 for c1 = 5, c2 = 7 (f(n) is Theta(n^2)).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sandwich Condition**: `c1 * g(n) <= f(n) <= c2 * g(n)`.
2. **Tightness Proof**: If upper and lower bounds match `g(n)`, `f(n)` is `Theta(g(n))`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `big_theta_verifier_demo()`: Solves Big-Theta Notation Tight Bound Verifier.

projects.title: Little-o vs Big-O Strict Upper Bound Profiler
projects.description: Little-o Notation `o(g(n))` represents a STRICT UPPER BOUND that is NOT asymptotically tight (e.g. `2n` is `o(n^2)`, but `3n^2` is NOT `o(n^2)`!). Limit definition: `lim_{n->inf} (f(n) / g(n)) = 0`. In this project, you will build Little-o Strict Upper Bound Profiler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Little-o Strict Upper Bounds, Limit Definitions `lim = 0` & Non-Tightness Proofs
projects.exampleText: Evaluate Little-o strict upper bound for f(n) = n and g(n) = n^2
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Little-o vs Big-O Strict Upper Bound Profiler ---
Limit as n->inf (n / n^2) = 0 → n is o(n^2) (Strictly small upper bound).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Limit Evaluation**: `L = lim_{n->inf} (f(n) / g(n))`.
2. **Little-o Condition**: If `L == 0`, `f(n)` is strictly smaller than `g(n)` (`o(g(n))`).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `little_o_profiler_demo()`: Solves Little-o vs Big-O Strict Upper Bound Profiler.

projects.title: Little-omega vs Big-Omega Strict Lower Bound Profiler
projects.description: Little-omega Notation `omega(g(n))` represents a STRICT LOWER BOUND that grows strictly faster than `g(n)`. Limit definition: `lim_{n->inf} (f(n) / g(n)) = infinity`. In this project, you will build Little-omega Strict Lower Bound Profiler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Little-omega Strict Lower Bounds, Infinity Limit Definitions & Growth Supremacy
projects.exampleText: Evaluate Little-omega strict lower bound for f(n) = n^2 and g(n) = n
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Little-omega vs Big-Omega Strict Lower Bound Profiler ---
Limit as n->inf (n^2 / n) = inf → n^2 is omega(n) (Strictly large lower bound).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Limit Evaluation**: `L = lim_{n->inf} (f(n) / g(n))`.
2. **Little-omega Condition**: If `L == infinity`, `f(n)` strictly dominates `g(n)` (`omega(g(n))`).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `little_omega_profiler_demo()`: Solves Little-omega vs Big-Omega Strict Lower Bound Profiler.

projects.title: Constant Time O(1) Operation Benchmark
projects.description: Constant Time `O(1)` algorithms execute in fixed runtime REGARDLESS of input size N. Benchmark array index lookup `arr[i]` or Hash Map lookup for `N = 10`, `N = 10,000`, and `N = 10,000,000` to prove flat 0-slope growth line! In this project, you will build Constant Time O(1) Benchmarker in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Constant Time O(1) Properties, Flat Growth Curves & Input Independent Execution
projects.exampleText: Benchmark execution time of O(1) operation across increasing N
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Constant Time O(1) Operation Benchmark ---
Execution time for N=10, N=10,000, N=10,000,000 is IDENTICAL (0.001 ms).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Flat Slope**: Execution time `T(N) = c` remains identical as N increases.
2. **O(1) Verification**: Variance across input sizes approaches 0.

projects.title: Logarithmic Time O(log N) Binary Search Growth Profiler
projects.description: Logarithmic Time `O(log N)` algorithms halve the subproblem size at every step (e.g. Binary Search, BST Search). Doubling input size N adds ONLY 1 extra operation step! Benchmark `N = 1,000` (10 steps) vs `N = 1,000,000` (20 steps). In this project, you will build Logarithmic Growth Profiler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Logarithmic O(log N) Halving Mechanics, Base-2 Logarithmic Slopes & Sub-Linear Speeds
projects.exampleText: Profile operation steps for O(log N) Binary Search across increasing N
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Logarithmic Time O(log N) Growth Profiler ---
Steps for N=1000 → 10 steps | N=1,000,000 → 20 steps (Logarithmic growth).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Halving Rule**: `N → N/2 → N/4 ... 1` takes `ceil(log2 N)` steps.
2. **Log Growth**: Multiplying N by 1,000 adds only ~10 steps.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `log_time_demo()`: Solves Logarithmic Time O(log N) Growth Profiler.

projects.title: Linear Time O(N) Array Scan Growth Profiler
projects.description: Linear Time `O(N)` algorithms process every element in input array once (e.g. linear search, array sum). Execution time increases in exact 1-to-1 direct proportion to input size N. In this project, you will build Linear Growth Profiler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Linear O(N) Direct Proportionality, 1-to-1 Scaling Slopes & Array Traversal Bounds
projects.exampleText: Profile execution time scaling for linear O(N) array scan
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Linear Time O(N) Array Scan Growth Profiler ---
Execution time scales 1-to-1 linearly with input size N.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Direct Proportion**: `T(k * N) = k * T(N)`.
2. **Linear Slope**: Doubling N doubles execution time.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `linear_time_demo()`: Solves Linear Time O(N) Array Scan Growth Profiler.

projects.title: Linearithmic Time O(N log N) Sorting Growth Profiler
projects.description: Linearithmic Time `O(N log N)` combines linear array scans with logarithmic subproblem splits (e.g. MergeSort, QuickSort, HeapSort). Represents the theoretical lower bound for comparison sorting! In this project, you will build Linearithmic Growth Profiler in C.

Execution time scales as N * log(N) (MergeSort / QuickSort growth).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Split-Merge Operations**: N elements processed across `log N` tree levels.
2. **Super-Linear Growth**: Grows slightly faster than pure linear O(N).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `linearithmic_time_demo()`: Solves Linearithmic Time O(N log N) Growth Profiler.

projects.title: Quadratic Time O(N^2) Nested Loop Growth Profiler
projects.description: Quadratic Time `O(N^2)` occurs in nested loops over N items (e.g. Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, 2D Grid sweeps). Doubling input size N QUADRUPLES execution time (`2^2 = 4x`). Benchmark steep quadratic growth curve! In this project, you will build Quadratic Growth Profiler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Quadratic O(N^2) Nested Loops, 4x Quadrupling Growth & Quadratic Explosion Profiling

projects.exampleOutput:
--- Quadratic Time O(N^2) Nested Loop Growth Profiler ---
Execution time quadruples when input size N is doubled.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Nested Loop Product**: Outer loop N x Inner loop N = `N^2` total iterations.
2. **Quadrupling Scaling**: `T(2N) = (2N)^2 = 4 N^2 = 4 T(N)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `quadratic_time_demo()`: Solves Quadratic Time O(N^2) Nested Loop Growth Profiler.

projects.title: Cubic Time O(N^3) Matrix Multiplication Growth Profiler
projects.description: Cubic Time `O(N^3)` occurs in 3-nested loops (e.g. naive `N x N` matrix multiplication, Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest paths). Doubling input size N causes an 8x INCREASE (`2^3 = 8x`) in runtime! In this project, you will build Cubic Growth Profiler in C.

Execution time increases by 8x when input size N is doubled.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Triple Loop**: 3 nested loops `i, j, k` execute `N * N * N = N^3` times.
2. **Octaling Growth**: `T(2N) = (2N)^3 = 8 N^3 = 8 T(N)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cubic_time_demo()`: Solves Cubic Time O(N^3) Matrix Multiplication Growth Profiler.

projects.title: Factorial Time O(N!) Permutation Generator Profiler
projects.description: Factorial Time `O(N!)` grows faster than any exponential function (e.g. brute-force Travelling Salesperson Problem, all permutations generation). `N=5 → 120`, `N=10 → 3.6 Million`, `N=15 → 1.3 Trillion`! In this project, you will build Factorial Growth Profiler in C.

projects.title: Asymptotic Dominance Ranking Tool
projects.description: Build an Asymptotic Dominance Ranking Engine that orders mathematical functions by asymptotic growth rate as `N → infinity`: `O(1) < O(log log N) < O(log N) < O(sqrt N) < O(N) < O(N log N) < O(N^2) < O(2^N) < O(N!)`. In this project, you will build Asymptotic Dominance Ranking Tool in C.

projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dominance Definition**: `f(n)` dominates `g(n)` if `lim_{n->inf} (g(n)/f(n)) = 0`.

projects.title: Empirical Step Counter vs Asymptotic Bound Auditor
projects.description: Compare exact step-counting formula `T(N) = 3N^2 + 5N + 2` against its asymptotic dominant term `Theta(N^2)`. Demonstrate why lower-order terms (`5N + 2`) become mathematically insignificant as `N → infinity`! In this project, you will build Step Counter Auditor in C.

projects.exampleText: Compare exact step formula T(N) = 3N^2 + 5N + 2 against Theta(N^2)

--- Empirical Step Counter vs Asymptotic Bound Auditor ---
Empirical Step Count Formula T(N) = 3N^2 + 5N + 2 | Asymptotic Dominant Term: Theta(N^2).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Lower Term Ratio**: As N grows, `(5N + 2) / (3N^2)` approaches 0.
2. **Asymptotic Simplification**: Drop constants and lower-order terms to yield `Theta(N^2)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `step_counter_auditor_demo()`: Solves Empirical Step Counter vs Asymptotic Bound Auditor.

projects.title: Constant Factor Masking Demonstration (Why O(100N) is O(N))
projects.description: Demonstrate why Big-O notation drops constant multipliers (e.g. `O(100 * N) == O(N)`). Show that while constant multiplier `100` affects CPU execution time on small inputs, the shape of the growth curve remains strictly LINEAR `O(N)` as `N → infinity`! In this project, you will build Constant Factor Masking Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Constant Multiplier Absorption, Constant Factor Masking & Curve Shape Invariants
projects.exampleText: Demonstrate why constant multiplier k=100 is dropped in O(100N) → O(N)
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Constant Factor Masking Demonstration (Why O(100N) is O(N)) ---
Proved that constant multiplier k=100 is absorbed by constant C in Big-O definition (c = 100).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Constant Absorption**: `f(n) = 100 n <= c * n` holds for `c = 100`.
2. **Rate of Growth**: Big-O measures rate of growth, not exact hardware instruction counts.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `constant_factor_masking_demo()`: Solves Constant Factor Masking Demonstration.

projects.title: Asymptotic Growth Crossing Point Calculator (n0 Threshold)
projects.description: Calculate the exact crossing point `n0` where a higher-order algorithm with small constant (e.g. `f1(n) = n^2`) becomes SLOWER than a lower-order algorithm with huge constant (e.g. `f2(n) = 1000 * n log2 n`). Find `n0` threshold! In this project, you will build Crossing Point Calculator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Crossing Point Threshold `n0`, Constant vs Order Trade-Offs & Algorithm Switching Bounds
projects.exampleText: Calculate crossing point n0 where f1(n) = n^2 exceeds f2(n) = 1000 * n log2 n
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Asymptotic Growth Crossing Point Calculator (n0 Threshold) ---
Calculated n0 = 44: For N < 44, O(N^2) algorithm runs FASTER than O(N log N) with huge constant!
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Intersection Equation**: Solve `n^2 = 1000 * n log2 n` for `n0`.
2. **Practical Threshold**: For `N < n0`, the simpler `O(N^2)` algorithm executes faster on CPU.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `n0_crossing_point_demo()`: Solves Asymptotic Growth Crossing Point Calculator.

projects.title: Limit Definition Solver for Asymptotic Notations
projects.description: Implement a limit definition solver for asymptotic notations: evaluate `L = lim_{n->inf} (f(n) / g(n))`. 1) If `L = 0`: `f is o(g)` and `O(g)`; 2) If `0 < L < inf`: `f is Theta(g)`; 3) If `L = inf`: `f is omega(g)` and `Omega(g)`! In this project, you will build Limit Definition Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Limit Definition of Asymptotic Notations, L'Hopital's Rule Math & Classification Engines
projects.exampleText: Classify asymptotic relation between f(n) and g(n) using limit definition
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Limit Definition Solver for Asymptotic Notations ---
Limit L = lim_{n->inf} (f(n)/g(n)): L=0 → o(g); 0<L<inf → Theta(g); L=inf → omega(g).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Limit Computation**: Evaluate `L = lim_{n->inf} (f(n) / g(n))` using numerical approximations or L'Hopital rule.
2. **Asymptotic Classification**: Map limit value `L` to exact Big-O, Theta, Omega, little-o, or little-omega relations.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `limit_definition_solver_demo()`: Solves Limit Definition Solver for Asymptotic Notations.

projects.title: Polylogarithmic vs Polynomial Growth Comparison Tool
projects.description: Prove that ANY polylogarithmic function `(log N)^k` is strictly dominated by ANY polynomial function `N^a` (for `a > 0`) as `N → infinity`. Benchmark `(log N)^10` vs `N^0.1` to demonstrate where polynomial growth overtakes polylogarithmic growth! In this project, you will build Polylog vs Polynomial Tool in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Polylogarithmic `(log N)^k` vs Fractional Polynomial `N^a`, Sub-Polynomial Growth Limits
projects.exampleText: Compare growth rates of polylogarithmic (log N)^10 vs fractional polynomial N^0.1
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Polylogarithmic vs Polynomial Growth Comparison Tool ---
Proved (log N)^10 is strictly dominated by N^0.1 for large N (Polylog < Polynomial).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Limit Proof**: `lim_{n->inf} ((log n)^k / n^a) = 0` for all `k > 0, a > 0`.
2. **Large N Crossing**: Compute huge `N` threshold where fractional polynomial overtakes high-power polylog.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `polylog_vs_poly_demo()`: Solves Polylogarithmic vs Polynomial Growth Comparison Tool.

projects.title: Parallel Multi-Threaded Asymptotic Scaling Engine
projects.description: Benchmark parallel multi-threaded asymptotic speedup scaling according to **Amdahl's Law** (`Speedup(P) = 1 / ((1 - S) + S / P)`). Profile parallel execution across 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 CPU cores to identify serial bottleneck fraction `S`! In this project, you will build Parallel Asymptotic Scaling Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Amdahl's Law Parallel Scaling, Serial Bottleneck Fraction `S` & Multi-Core Speedups

projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Amdahl's Formula**: `Speedup(P) = 1 / ((1 - S) + S / P)` where `S` is parallelizable fraction.
2. **Serial Limit**: Maximum theoretical speedup bounded by `1 / (1 - S)` regardless of P.
